title: Operationalizing Pluralistic Values in Large Language Model Alignment Reveals Trade-offs in Safety, Inclusivity, and Model Behavior

bias_targets.methodology: Generating model responses to gender-related prompts and collecting human evaluations on a 5-point Likert scale to measure 'Stereotypical Bias' (beliefs about a person's abilities and interests based on their gender).

Fine-tuning language models on preference data stratified by the political orientation of raters (Liberal vs. Conservative) and evaluating the resulting models to measure whose values are prioritized in downstream emotional awareness and toxicity.

Fine-tuning language models on preference data stratified by rater ethnicity (White vs. Black) and evaluating the differences in the models' emotional awareness to highlight disparities in value alignment.

Comparing alignment outcomes across different disagreement aggregation strategies (e.g., majority vote vs. preserving all ratings) to evaluate how standard alignment pipelines suppress minority viewpoints and enforce an algorithmic monoculture.
